title: BFS And DFS Scrolling Review
summary: Short traversal concepts, implementation reminders, code snippets, and interview prompts for mobile review.
audience: Developers learning graph traversal or preparing BFS and DFS coding interview patterns.

cards.title: BFS Uses A Queue
cards.prompt: Breadth-first search expands nodes in first-in, first-out discovery order.
cards.explanation: The queue preserves distance layers, so every node d edges away is expanded before any node d plus one edges away.

cards.title: DFS Uses A Stack
cards.prompt: Depth-first search follows one branch before it backtracks.
cards.explanation: Recursion uses the runtime call stack; iterative DFS makes the same pending path explicit with a stack collection.

cards.title: Visited Prevents Cycles
cards.prompt: A general graph traversal needs a record of nodes already discovered.
cards.explanation: Without visited state, a cycle can repeat forever and shared neighbors can be processed many times.

cards.title: Shortest Often Means BFS
cards.prompt: Equal-cost moves plus a minimum-step question are the classic BFS signal.
cards.explanation: BFS explores increasing path lengths. The first target discovery is optimal when every edge has the same cost.

cards.title: Weights Change The Algorithm
cards.prompt: Plain BFS does not solve shortest paths with different edge costs.
cards.explanation: The layer number counts edges, not total weight. Nonnegative weighted paths usually call for Dijkstra's algorithm.

cards.title: Mark Before Enqueue
cards.prompt: Mark a BFS neighbor visited at the moment it enters the queue.
cards.explanation: Early marking prevents two parents in the same frontier from enqueueing the same shared neighbor.

cards.title: TypeScript Queue Head
cards.prompt: Advance a head index instead of repeatedly shifting an array-backed queue.
cards.explanation: The array keeps queued values while head identifies the next item, avoiding repeated front removal and reindexing.

cards.title: Python Queue Pop
cards.prompt: Python deque provides efficient removal from the front of the BFS queue.
cards.explanation: Use popleft for FIFO order; list pop without an index removes from the end and behaves like a stack.
cards.code:
from collections import deque
queue = deque([start])
node = queue.popleft()

cards.title: Depth Can Break Recursion
cards.prompt: Use iterative DFS when graph depth is large or controlled by untrusted input.
cards.explanation: An explicit stack preserves DFS behavior without depending on the runtime's limited recursive call stack.

cards.title: Grid Becomes A Graph
cards.prompt: In Number Of Islands, what are the vertices, edges, and connected components?
cards.explanation: Land cells are vertices, orthogonal land adjacencies are edges, and each maximal connected component is one island.

cards.title: Two Correct Island Traversals
cards.prompt: BFS and DFS both count islands in O(rows times cols) time.
cards.explanation: The prompt needs complete component discovery, so internal traversal order does not change the count; memory shape and recursion safety differ.

cards.title: DFS Finds Back Edges
cards.prompt: A prerequisite edge to a node on the active DFS path proves a directed cycle.
cards.explanation: The visiting color means that dependency has not finished; reaching it again closes a cycle in the active chain.

cards.title: Kahn Starts At Zero
cards.prompt: BFS topological processing begins with every course whose indegree is zero.
cards.explanation: Removing ready courses can make dependents ready. A cycle leaves some courses with positive indegree forever.

cards.title: Both Are Linear
cards.prompt: Adjacency-list BFS and DFS both take O(V + E) time with visited tracking.
cards.explanation: Every reachable vertex is processed once, and every adjacency-list edge is inspected a constant number of times.

cards.title: Shape Drives Memory
cards.prompt: BFS stores a frontier; DFS stores an active path and pending branches.
cards.explanation: Wide graphs pressure a BFS queue, while deep graphs pressure a DFS stack even though both have O(V) worst-case space.

cards.title: Explain Before Coding
cards.prompt: State the node, edge, visited rule, and traversal invariant before implementation.
cards.explanation: A precise model turns a story problem into a standard traversal and gives the interviewer a clear correctness argument.
